Essential Terminology & Concepts

A stack is one of the most fundamental abstract data structures in computer programming.

Array Implementation Of Lists Key Concept

In Python programming, queues store and manipulate elements in a FIFO (First-In-First-Out) manner.

Linked Lists-Implementation Key Concept

A double-ended queue, commonly referred to as a deque, allows insertion and removal of elements from both ends, making it a hybrid between stacks and queues.

📌 Key Takeaways

Section-by-Section Study Breakdown

6.2 Abstract Data Type-List

  • A stack is one of the most fundamental abstract data structures in computer programming.
  • We add and remove the elements from the same end of the stack which follows Last-in-first-out (LIFO) principle.
  • Understanding stacks is crucial for many programming applications, from managing program execution to implementing undo operations in applications.
  • Understanding Stacks A stack can be visualized as a vertical list of elements.

6.3 Array Implementation of Lists

  • In Python programming, queues store and manipulate elements in a FIFO (First-In-First-Out) manner.
  • Unlike static data structures, queues provide dynamic and flexible mechanisms for managing ordered collections where the first element is the first one to be removed.
  • Queues are essential in various programming scenarios, particularly in managing tasks, scheduling processes, and handling asynchronous data.
  • In this section, we will discuss the queue data structure in Python, covering its implementation, key operations, best practices, and practical use cases.

6.4 Linked Lists-Implementation

  • A double-ended queue, commonly referred to as a deque, allows insertion and removal of elements from both ends, making it a hybrid between stacks and queues.
  • In this section, we will explore the deque data structure in Python, including its implementation, key operations, best practices, and practical use cases.
  • Understanding Deques A deque can be visualized as a linear collection of elements where you can add or remove items from both ends.
  • The primary operations associated with deques include: - Append: Adding an element to the back of the deque.

6.5 Doubly Linked Lists-Implementation
